A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hypnotic depth, as measured by the PCI-HAP, is associated with the following processes: (1) the ability to experience trance state phenomena; (2) the ability to be suggestible to the hypnotic induction and to suggestions; (3) the expectancy that one will respond to the induction and to suggestions (both estimated and expected therapeutic efficacy); and (4) the ability to remain in a hypnotic state (as measured by eye catalepsy).
the self-report of hypnotic depth is a function of several of the processes associated with hypnotic trance, including altered states, suggestibility, and expectancies.
the srHD is an amalgamation of the effects of suggestibility, expectation, and trance state effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self-reporting hypnotic depth is a complex function of many component processes.
the PCI-HAP can be used to predict the self-reported depth of hypnosis, which is an important component of hypnotic ability.
the PCI-HAP can be used for the assessment of the component processes of suggestibility, expectancy, and trance state and catalepsy effects in hypnotic depth.
